html:
"Gharra" is the map's name, from 1530 to 1700, for the inland desert of central and southern Oman, between the Omani heartland around the Hajar Mountains and Dhofar in the south. The name is hard to match to any known state, and it may be a garbled label in the source data.

The land is gravel desert on the edge of the Empty Quarter, home to Bedouin camel herders, tribes such as the Harasis, Janaba and Duru, who were loosely tied to the rulers of Muscat and to the imams of the interior. In these years the Yaruba imams united Oman. To the west lay the Mahra Sultanate.
